national.title: Two Italians killed in strike in Kuwait, as Iran denies responsibility
national.summary: The pair were technicians for German company Rheinmetall, according to Italy's foreign ministry.
national.body:
Two Italian nationals have died following a strike on a facility in Kuwait which both countries have blamed on Iran.

The pair were technicians working for German arms manufacturing company Rheinmetall, Italy's foreign ministry said.

Iran has denied responsibility for the attack, with armed forces spokesperson Abolfazl Shekarchi saying "no military or offensive operations have been conducted" by its military.

Kuwait's defence ministry said earlier that four people - the two Italians, a Kuwaiti national and Pakistani national - had been injured from falling shrapnel after a number of drones from Iran were detected and intercepted.

It comes just over a week after Kuwait said it had repelled overnight Iranian drone attacks on an airbase which hosts US forces - the first strikes in more than two months on the country.

Recent exchanges of fire between the US and Iran, and a deadlock in negotiations, have raised fears of a major escalation in the war.

The conflict began when US and Israel attacked Iran in late February, with Iran retaliating by launching missiles and drones at Israel and Gulf Arab states hosting US military assets and personnel.

Iranian-backed militias in the region have also carried out attacks on the US's Gulf allies.

national.title: Andy Taylor, guitarist of new wave icons Duran Duran, dies at 65
national.summary: Andy Taylor, the original guitarist of the 1980s English new wave band Duran Duran, whose huge pop hits included "Hungry Like the Wolf," "The Reflex" and "Rio" and were inextricably linked to the launch of MTV, has died. He was 65.
national.body:
Mark Kennedy, Associated Press Mark Kennedy, Associated Press

Andy Taylor, the original guitarist of the 1980s English new wave band Duran Duran, whose huge pop hits included "Hungry Like the Wolf," "The Reflex" and "Rio" and were inextricably linked to the launch of MTV, has died. He was 65.

Taylor's death was confirmed by his family and bandmates in a statement posted on social media and Duran Duran's website.

"From the moment he arrived in Birmingham from the North East with a guitar and an unshakeable belief in what we could become, he brought an indelible fire and swagger to our music. His playing drove the songs that took us around the world, and with a dry wit that was matched only by his wonderfully unsentimental, no-nonsense outlook on life he kept us grounded and gave the band its edge through the extraordinary years that followed," the band said.

On the night he was inducted into the Rock & Roll Hall of Fame in November 2022, Taylor revealed that he had been battling Stage 4 metastatic prostate cancer for several years and was unable to attend.

"I would like to thank each of my brothers in this great band," he wrote. "You can dream about what happened to us but to experience it, on one's own terms, as mates, was beyond incredible."

The two-time Grammy Award-winners had nine gold records and six platinum ones, with 20 Top 20 singles in the U.K. and 18 in the U.S. They were two-time Ivor Novello Award winners and are MTV Video Visionary Award recipients.

The band's 1981 debut album "Duran Duran" had their first hit single, "Planet Earth," but it was "Rio" that transformed them into trans-Atlantic stars. The Rock Hall explained their appeal this way: "They were new wave outsiders who became music video stars — 'Tiger Beat' fashion pinups who rocked arenas."

national.title: Fake online stores may fool AI shopping bots on Black Friday
national.summary: AI bots are accidentally steering shoppers toward websites and online shops created by scammers using AI.
national.body: Scammers are using AI to churn out convincing copies of real online stores, and this Black Friday, the AI agents that many shoppers will rely on often can't tell the difference.These fake sites pose a risk to the millions of Americans who are tasking their AI agents with making online purchases and transacting on their behalf. "Artificial intelligence just makes building websites so much easier. You can upload anything into HTML and build a website very, very easily," Harrison Tang, co-founder of Spokeo, a data aggregator, told CBS News.AI is enabling scammers to build what Tang described as convincing dupes of legitimate online stores in only hours, including copies of a brand's logo, marketing language and product images and descriptions."AI just makes creating these look-alike fake stores a lot easier, so there is a proliferation of them," Tang explained. "Platforms will try to catch them by not directing users there, but there are so many of them popping up all the time that they are hard to keep up with." Research from Microsoft shows that criminals can use AI to set up fraudulent e-commerce sites in mere minutes rather than the days or weeks that were once required.Spokeo identified copycat sites of dozens of popular brands, including UGG, L.L. Bean, Converse and Stella McCartney. As of Nov. 15, it had identified 65 distinct online stores that mimicked the legitimate sites of 60 brand names, according to its online shopping scam study. The discrepancies between the authentic stores and the scam websites are subtle and require close examination. The first place to look for proof of fraud, according to Tang, is in the online store's web address. For example, a fake Converse store uses the web address converseshop.us.com, whereas the real store's address is converse.com. The .us domain name is the top-level domain for the U.S. and is reserved for U.S. residents, but is commonly used for phishing attempts, according to Tang. "It looks like an official website, but it's not, so if you don't pay close attention, it's easy to get tricked," he said. AI agents need to get savvyBots aren't as well trained as some humans are at spotting phony websites, which can dupe even discerning shoppers because of how realistic they look. national.summary: German police arrested two Iraqi men alleged to be members of an Iran-linked terrorist organization​ that is said to have targeted U.S., Israeli and Jewish institutions in Europe.
national.body: Berlin — German authorities on Thursday arrested two Iraqi men on suspicion of terrorism. The suspects are alleged to be members of an Iran-linked terrorist organization that is said to have targeted U.S., Israeli and Jewish institutions in Europe.The men, who were arrested in Cologne and Heidelberg by the Federal Criminal Police Office, are Iraqi nationals Mostafa Al-R. and Ameer J., according to the Federal Public Prosecutor's Office.The investigation centers on alleged links to Harakat Ashab al-Yamin al-Islamiya, a shadowy group that emerged to claim a series of sabotage, arson and violent attacks targeting Jewish institutions in Europe not long after the start of the U.S. war with Iran. The U.S. government has labeled HAYI a front for Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps and the Iran-backed militia Kataib Hezbollah in Iraq. Britain has designated HAYI as a terrorist organization.According to investigators, Mostafa Al-R. is alleged to have maintained contact with Mohammad Al-Saadi, who is currently facing criminal charges in the United States. Al-Saadi is considered a central figure within the alleged terrorist network.As early as late 2025, Al-Saadi, Mostafa Al-R. and other individuals allegedly founded an independent group whose goal was to carry out terrorist attacks in Germany and other European countries, according to prosecutors. Ameer J. is also a member of this group, they said.The group planned to target synagogues in Cologne and another European city, prosecutors alleged, saying unknown perpetrators traveled to the locations in March 2026 on behalf of the organization. The plans were not implemented for unknown reasons.HAYI is also linked to attacks on Jewish institutions in the United Kingdom, France, Belgium and the Netherlands, the Federal Office for the Protection of the Constitution said.The suspects are accused of membership in a domestic terrorist organization under Section 129a of Germany's Criminal Code. The investigating judge at the Federal Court of Justice had already issued the corresponding arrest warrants on Nov. 18.Along with the arrests, extensive searches took place in Baden-Württemberg, Hesse and North Rhine-Westphalia. A total of 17 locations were searched. national.title: Elon Musk doubles SpaceX share pledge for U.S. children
national.summary: Every child in the U.S. will receive one share of SpaceX from the company and one from Elon Musk.
national.body: Elon Musk is upping a pledge to kickstart U.S. children's savings. On Wednesday, Musk and SpaceX said they will give every U.S. child two shares in the space exploration company, doubling a pledge the world's richest person made in October, which he said at the time would be the "first of many" planned gifts. In the statement, SpaceX said it would give each child a newly issued share of its Class A common stock. The company will contribute the shares to U.S. kids' Trump Accounts, tax-advantaged investment accounts the White House created to help American children build long-term savings. Musk will personally match the number of shares SpaceX donates, according to Thursday's statement. Additionally, SpaceX president and chief operating officer Gwynne Shotwell will donate more than 2 million SpaceX shares to U.S. children.The total giveaway is worth about $18 billion, based on SpaceX's most recent stock price. "SpaceX is building the infrastructure of the future and working to make life multiplanetary," the company said in announcing the donation. "We believe ownership of the company creating these systems should extend to the next generation of Americans for their long-term benefit."There are roughly 70 million children in the U.S. who are eligible for a Trump Account. The Trump administration is automatically enrolling kids under eighteen with a valid Social Security number in the program. However, parents or guardians must still claim their child's account for it to be active. As of Tuesday, friends and family members had contributed more than $1 billion to individual Trump Accounts, according to Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent. Additionally, philanthropists including Michael and Susan Dell and other donors have made major gifts, bringing the total assets deposited in Trump Accounts to over $9 billion.

national.title: French cinema star Gérard Depardieu ordered to stand trial for rape and sexual assault
national.summary: Gérard Depardieu, for decades one of France's most celebrated actors, has been ordered to stand trial on charges of raping and sexually assaulting a young actress, authorities said Thursday, less than two weeks after the cinema star abandoned his appeal of a sexual assault conviction in a separate c
national.body:
Thomas Adamson, Associated Press Thomas Adamson, Associated Press

PARIS (AP) — Gérard Depardieu, for decades one of France's most celebrated actors, has been ordered to stand trial on charges of raping and sexually assaulting a young actress, authorities said Thursday, less than two weeks after the cinema star abandoned his appeal of a sexual assault conviction in a separate case.

Actress Charlotte Arnould was 22 when she accused Depardieu in 2018 of raping her at his Paris home.

Eight years later, the Paris Court of Appeal ruled that the actor should face trial over allegations of rape and sexual assault on Aug. 7, 2018, while dismissing allegations relating to a second incident six days later.

Depardieu, 77, has denied the rape allegations. His lawyer, Delphine Meillet, told The Associated Press that he disputes Thursday's ruling, without specifying whether he would challenge it before France's highest court for civil and criminal cases.

The ruling upholds part of an investigating judge's August 2025 decision to send Depardieu to trial.

The case has become one of the most prominent in France's reckoning with sexual violence, as the #MeToo movement has faced resistance in the country, particularly in the arts.

With his hulking frame, crooked nose and commanding screen presence, Depardieu dominated French cinema for half a century.

national.summary: President Donald Trump, who has staked his economic policy on growth in the artificial intelligence sector, will travel to Arizona on Dec. 4 to speak at the groundbreaking for a new Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co. computer chip foundry, according to both the White House and the Taiwan-based c
national.body:
WEST PALM BEACH, Fla. (AP) — President Donald Trump, who has staked his economic policy on growth in the artificial intelligence sector, will travel to Arizona on Dec. 4 to speak at the groundbreaking for a new Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co. computer chip foundry, according to both the White House and the Taiwan-based company.

The trip will come at the end of a week where AI comes under the microscope in Washington in the aftermath of Trump intervening to get his ally Jensen Huang reinstated as CEO of Nvidia. Huang is slated to testify at a Senate Banking Committee hearing on Dec. 3 and will face questions about how his company has been selling its chips abroad — and his affair with a woman suspected of being a Chinese spy. Beijing has denied it.

WATCH: How Trump may have profited from Huang's return to Nvidia

TSMC has expanded aggressively in the Phoenix, Arizona, area, using its U.S. facilities to manufacture chips for tech companies such as Nvidia, Apple, AMD, Broadcom, and Qualcomm. Trump is attending the start of construction on the fifth phase of TSMC's expansion in Arizona.

TSMC in July announced plans to spend another $100 billion on expanding its manufacturing capacity in the United States, bringing its total pledged investment in American chipmaking to $265 billion.

WATCH: U.S. works to close loophole that let China access advanced AI chips

The size of the investment has grown as the development of artificial intelligence has stimulated demand for more computer chips, at the same time as Taiwan's dominance in chipmaking has led countries including the U.S. to address supply chain vulnerabilities by producing more domestically.

While Trump has sought to promote the investments as a function of his tariffs, the company began construction in Arizona during the presidency of Democrat Joe Biden. The bipartisan CHIPS and Science Act, signed into law by Biden, also helped to provide some financial support for the project.

national.title: Texas band raises $350,000 to stay for Macy's Thanksgiving parade
national.summary: Other marching bands from around the U.S. are also raising funds to cover the cost of staying in New York City after the parade was rescheduled for Saturday.
national.body: One high school marching band from Texas says it has raised $350,000 to cover the cost of its 500-member group remaining in New York City after the Macy's Thanksgiving Day Parade was rescheduled until Saturday due to a potentially historic storm hitting the region on Thursday."It's been exhausting and emotional to figure this out, but it has been incredibly humbling to see an outpouring of kindness," Ryan Demkovich, the director of the Pride of Pearland Marching Band at Pearland High School in Texas, told CBS News about raising the funds required to cover the extended trip.Other marching bands that traveled to New York from across the country are also raising money to cover the cost of their extended stays. For many of the high school musicians, the parade is a once-in-a-lifetime chance to perform for millions of spectators along the route and watching at home, and the postponement has made the trip significantly more expensive."This was quite a challenge for us, and there was a very frantic and large call to action to our community to let the kids stay here and finish it out," Demkovich added. By Thursday, the band had raised enough money to pay for two extra nights at a hotel and to charter buses back to Texas after the parade on Saturday. One logistical challenge: They'll have to relocate from the Marriott Marquis in Times Square, which is booked for the weekend, to a hotel near the Meadowlands Sports Complex in New Jersey. And they'll travel home by bus on Saturday because flights are booked until late Monday or Tuesday, Demkovich said. The donations also cover extra meals for the ensemble. The parade's delay also scrambled plans for tourists and family members who had traveled to New York to see the parade on Thursday. national.title: More than 1,000 flights cancelled or delayed in US as weather disrupts Thanksgiving travel
national.summary: Massive storms are descending on both US coasts as an estimated 80 million Americans hit the road for Thanksgiving holiday.
national.body:
Nearly 400 flights in the US have been cancelled so far on Thursday as bad weather coincides with busy travel on the Thanksgiving holiday.

Another 1,200 flights into, out of, or within the US have been delayed, tracking site FlightAware said.

On Wednesday, the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) briefly grounded all flights heading for Miami International Airport after a FedEx aircraft overran a runway. No injuries were reported, and the FAA is investigating.

More than 80 million Americans were expected to be traveling this week at the same time the National Weather Service (NWS) has forecast storms along the western and eastern coasts of the US that could bring heavy rain and flooding.

The FAA previously warned that delays across the country would be possible "throughout the week" as a result of the rain and wind that are forecast. On Wednesday, FlightAware reported more than 6,800 delays and more than 160 cancellations.

The NWS forecast a strong storm will deluge the eastern US coast on Thursday, bringing high winds, heavy rainfall and major coastal flooding.

Ahead of expected severe weather in New Jersey, the state's governor, Mikie Sherrill, declared a state of emergency. Several coastal areas that experienced flooding earlier this autumn could be vulnerable again on Thursday.

In New York City, organisers of the annual Macy's Thanksgiving parade have postponed the event to Saturday.

national.title: Zelenskyy warns of imminent major Russian attack on Ukraine's power grid
national.summary: Russia is preparing another major attack on Ukraine's energy infrastructure, logistics and critical services, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said Thursday, as U.S. envoy Jared Kushner said Russian President Vladimir Putin has "shown restraint" in the war by agreeing not to use nuclear weapo
national.body:
Samya Kullab, Associated Press Samya Kullab, Associated Press

Elise Morton, Associated Press Elise Morton, Associated Press

KYIV, Ukraine (AP) — Russia is preparing another major attack on Ukraine's energy infrastructure, logistics and critical services, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said Thursday, as U.S. envoy Jared Kushner said Russian President Vladimir Putin has "shown restraint" in the war by agreeing not to use nuclear weapons.

Kushner, who is mediating Russia-Ukraine talks with envoy Steve Witkoff, said that after talking at length with Putin, he believes the Russian leader wants peace almost five years after Moscow invaded Ukraine.

Putin "has agreed not to use nuclear weapons, which obviously is a big thing, and he's reassured us that that's not his intention," Kushner said on the MD Meets podcast by Axel Springer Creators.

The son-in-law of U.S. President Donald Trump added that "what (Putin) is saying is peace, but I think it's always peace on what terms" as the talks have hit "a little bit of a deadlock" over the fate of Ukrainian territory.

Zelenskyy and European leaders have criticized Putin for what they describe as Moscow's refusal to compromise and determination to press on with an invasion that has killed hundreds of thousands of troops and thousands of Ukrainian civilians.

Putin wants a new relationship with Washington, according to Kushner, as Russia seeks to keep NATO away from its borders.

national.title: Food banks see influx of families ahead of Thanksgiving
national.summary: Across the U.S., volunteers have noticed more families than usual seeking food assistance as people struggle with higher grocery costs.
national.body: Thousands of cars inched across the massive parking lot outside AT&T Stadium on Nov. 20, where the Dallas Cowboys are set to play the Eagles Thursday afternoon.But it had nothing to do with football.Instead of tailgating, volunteers filled up families' trunks with turkeys, potatoes, cabbage, carrots and more."The demand is bigger than I expected," said Julie Butner, the president and CEO of Tarrant Area Food Bank. a not-for-profit organization serving 13 counties in North Texas.They expected 4,000 families to come out to their annual mega market, but had to bring in more food when more than 5,400 families showed up, she said.And the first car of the day had been lined up since 10:00 p.m. the night before."That tells us they need food," Butner said, "Who does that unless they're hungry?"From Florida to California, food banks are seeing an influx of families.In Virginia, an estimated 3,000 families showed up at food banks."We've given away more food than we ever have in the past," Virginia State Senator Mike Jones said. The surge can be attributed to a Thanksgiving meal costing 6% more this year, according to the American Farm Bureau Federation, and to the more than 5 million Americans who lost food assistance since the "One Big Beautiful Bill Act" became law in July 2025. "It's either groceries, or you know, we get a pair of shoes," said Lauren Sevier, a Texas mom of four boys, who's hoping to make her Thanksgiving food stretch beyond the holiday. She called the Tarrant Area Food Bank's event the "biggest blessing."If you're struggling to put food on the table during this holiday season, dial 211 and you'll get connected with local resources on free meals, food banks and more. Also go to feedingamerica.org for more resources.

national.summary: The Massachusetts State Lottery posted on social media last week a photo of Ariel Velasquez-Morales, who won $1 million from a scratch-off ticket purchased in Boston.
national.body: Immigration officials detained a man in Massachusetts this week days after he won $1 million from a scratch-off lottery ticket, U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement said Wednesday.The Massachusetts State Lottery posted on social media last week a photo of Ariel Velasquez-Morales, who won $1 million from a scratch-off ticket purchased in Boston. A few days later, ICE reposted the smiling photo of Velasquez-Morales and said he had been detained.According to a statement from ICE, Velasquez-Morales entered the U.S. illegally from El Salvador in 2013, and an immigration judge in 2014 ordered his removal.ICE said Velasquez-Morales is being detained pending removal from the country. It's unclear where he is being held.ICE's Boston office also posted the photo of Velasquez-Morales and wrote, "Welcome to the ERO Boston lottery! For over a year, Abrego Garcia and the Trump administration fought over his removal, with the administration seeking to deport him to various African countries while Abrego Garcia said he would voluntarily leave for Costa Rica.Speaking from Spain on Wednesday, Abrego Garcia said, "The government did not decide where my story continues." national.title: Trump calls GDP figures 'fake' and demands an investigation of Commerce Department
national.summary: President Donald Trump on Thursday accused his Commerce Department of purposely issuing incorrect economic growth figures before the midterm elections, and said he wants to launch an investigation.
national.body:
WEST PALM BEACH, Fla. (AP) — President Donald Trump on Thursday accused his Commerce Department of purposely issuing incorrect economic growth figures before the midterm elections, and said he wants to launch an investigation.

Trump has repeatedly sought to undermine trust in economic data that fails to match his claims of a historic boom, a pattern that threatens the credibility of figures needed by businesses, financial markets and consumers when making investments.

His latest complaint concerns data issued by the Commerce Department on Wednesday that revised gross domestic product in the third quarter to 4.3% on an annual basis, up from a prior estimate of 3.4%.

The department's Bureau of Economic Analysis routinely updates its economic data to improve their accuracy. GDP figures, monthly jobs reports and other data are regularly revised. Those updates occur on a pre-scheduled basis without regard to the political calendar.

But the president claimed on social media that it was a "massive, and purposeful, error" and linked it to the poor performance for Republicans in the Nov. 3 midterm elections that gave Democrats control of both houses of Congress.

"It was just revealed that the REAL Numbers on the Economy, published before the Election, were FAKE, and a correction was issued yesterday by the people in the Government Agency that does these numbers," Trump posted. "Why wasn't the correct number issued before the Election? I am asking for an immediate investigation of this situation."

WATCH: How Trump's newest tariffs could impact Americans and the economy

The Commerce Department did not immediately respond to a request for comment. The government is largely closed on Thursday for the Thanksgiving holiday.

national.title: Nine injured, three critically, after Bangkok oil refinery explosion
national.summary: Black smoke could be seen across Bangkok's skyline after the blast, as officials urged residents to leave the area.
national.body:
Nine people have been injured after an explosion at an oil refinery in Bangkok, authorities have said.

Three of them are in critical condition, according to news agency AFP, which said the local hospital had revised its earlier assessment of four.

A fire broke out after the blast at the Phra Khanong facility run by energy giant Bangchak Corporation in the east of Thailand's capital at around 14:45 (07:45 GMT).

The company said the fire was brought under control and put out within 30 minutes, adding that the cause of the incident was being investigated.

Black smoke could be seen across Bangkok's skyline after the blast, as local officials told residents to leave the area.

An alert sent to mobile phones by Bangkok authorities confirmed that the fire was under control, but urged people to avoid the area.

Eyewitnesses shared video clips on social media of flames and smoke rising above the refinery.

On a visit to the scene, Thailand's energy minister Akanat Promphan said it appeared the impact of the explosion was limited because the fire started in a distillation tower about 100m (330ft) from where oil was being stored.

national.title: Could the Black Sea pull the U.S. into war in Europe?
national.summary: The Russia-Ukraine war is spilling into the Black Sea, where violent incidents have surged, running right up to NATO's doorstep.
national.body: Constanța, Romania – Out on the Black Sea, the Romanian Navy is always on the lookout for the deadly debris of a war it isn't fighting.It's a front of the Russia-Ukraine war that most people rarely see. It runs right up to NATO's doorstep and sometimes crosses into its waters — threatening to pull the alliance, and therefore the United States, into the war.Incidents involving drones, mines and commercial ships are surging in the Black Sea, NATO military spokesperson Colonel Martin O'Donnell told CBS News."In 2025, for example, we saw fewer than 50 incidents in the Black Sea. This year alone, we're talking four to five hundred," he said.The roughly tenfold increase threatens a major artery of global grain and fuel shipments and has made the waterway deadlier than the Strait of Hormuz, a flashpoint in the U.S.-Iran war, with both sides trying to enforce blockades on the chokepoint to exert economic pressure on the other.Twenty-five sailors have been killed in the strait this year, according to the International Maritime Organization, while at least 40 have been killed in the Black Sea in the same period, according to the International Transport Workers' Federation."I would say the Black Sea is just as important, and then depending on who you talk to, some might argue could perhaps even be more important … in terms of global trade," said O'Donnell.Any imbalance in the flow of fuel and food "can have global implications that can impact America just as much as it can any of the nations here," he said.And this maritime front stretches beyond the Black Sea.Over the weekend, Ukraine said it struck an advanced Russian warship and a cargo ship that then drifted, on fire, into the waters of NATO member Finland.On Sunday, Ukraine said it sank a Russian warship docked in Libya.Three of the six countries bordering the Black Sea are NATO members — Romania, Bulgaria and Turkey.But as Romanian Navy Captain Mihai Iordache explains, defending those borders is nothing like defending them on land."We do not have a fence into the Black Sea to state this is our border, that is the other border," he said.The Romanian Navy is deploying highly specialized divers and drones, scouring the depths for unexploded weapons.All this comes as the pressure on NATO is mounting. national.title: Judge blocks FCC from early license review for ABC, which network says has had a chilling effect
national.summary: A federal judge on Wednesday blocked the Federal Communications Commission from conducting an early review of ABC's broadcast licenses, agreeing with the network that the Trump administration was chilling the network's free speech rights.
national.body:
Michael Kunzelman, Associated Press Michael Kunzelman, Associated Press

WASHINGTON (AP) — A federal judge on Wednesday blocked the Federal Communications Commission from conducting an early review of ABC's broadcast licenses, agreeing with the network that the Trump administration was chilling the network's free speech rights.

U.S. District Judge Loren AliKhan in Washington, D.C., granted ABC's request for a temporary restraining order and a preliminary injunction on First Amendment grounds. The network accuses the FCC of violating its free speech rights in retaliation against programming decisions that the Trump administration dislikes.

AliKhan noted in her ruling that the network was likely to succeed on its First Amendment claim.

AliKhan, who was nominated by former President Joe Biden, said ABC had detailed "a campaign of retaliation against them in response to their exercise of their First Amendment rights," which on its own is an 'irreparable injury.'"

ABC and its parent company, Disney, sued the FCC and FCC Commissioner Brendan Carr in August, several months after the commission ordered eight ABC-owned stations to submit renewal applications for their broadcast licenses years ahead of schedule.

"Today's decision is an important victory for the First Amendment," a spokesperson for ABC News said in a statement.

An FCC spokesperson said in a statement that the part of the decision granting ABC's motion "is wrong on the facts and wrong on the law," adding that the agency "looks forward to prevailing in full on this matter."

national.title: King tides and strong waves destroy part of Pacifica pier as officials warn of coastal flooding
national.summary: King tides combined with powerful waves destroyed part of a pier in Northern California on Wednesday, and officials warned more beachfront homes are at risk of flooding.
national.body:
SAN FRANCISCO (AP) — King tides combined with powerful waves destroyed part of a pier in Northern California on Wednesday, and officials warned more beachfront homes are at risk of flooding.

A video showed a massive wave tearing down a portion of the pier in the city of Pacifica and slamming it into the ocean. Officials had closed the L-shaped, 1,140 feet-long (350 meters-long) pier in the summer after finding cracks in the structure.

Beachfront homes in the city south of San Francisco began flooding this week as king tides, the highest tides of the year, arrived in the area.

North of San Francisco, Marin County officials issued an evacuation warning for residents of beachfront properties in Stinson Beach, saying large waves expected through the afternoon could send water and debris into roads and homes. The warning was lifted later Wednesday but authorities advised people to stay away from the beach as large waves continue to pound the area.

The National Weather Service issued a coastal flood warning for the Pacific Coast and bay shorelines along San Francisco Bay and San Pablo Bay through 4 p.m. Wednesday. It also issued a high surf warning in the Bay Area for Wednesday, when breaking waves of 20 to 30 feet (6 to 9 meters), about two to three stories high, could overpower swimmers and sweep people into the ocean.

WATCH: News Wrap: Severe weather threatens holiday travel for millions

"Rising tides will bring water and waves farther up the beach than normal, restricting escape from beaches and coastal area," the weather service said.

King tides occur when the gravitational pull of the moon and sun aligns to raise water levels. Their effects this year are being amplified by the ongoing super El Niño, which has warmed the ocean, leading to an increased volume of seawater.

national.title: New UK-EU treaty has 10-year termination clause
national.summary: Text of the treaties was published this afternoon, alongside legislation designed to enact the bulk of the deal.
national.body:
Economics editor Published 26 November 2026, 02:13 GMT Updated 4 hours ago The government and the EU have published the texts of two treaties agreed last week as part of a post-Brexit reset.

The treaties were published on Thursday afternoon, alongside legislation designed to enact the bulk of the deal.

The deal covering food exports has a 10-year termination clause that would mean if one party ended the agreement, they would have to pay "reasonable and proportionate costs" to rebuild border checks infrastructure, which will be significantly scaled back as part of the new deal.

Opposition leader Kemi Badenoch has said she would scrap the deal while Reform UK's Nigel Farage has suggested he would refuse to pay.

The Brexit reset deal has already sparked debate about its benefits, its costs, and a wider discussion on the future of the UK-EU relationship.

The deal covers British food exports, emissions trading and a youth experience scheme.

Two of the three legal texts were released on Thursday, covering the food trade and emissions trading scheme deals, alongside the government's cost-cutting bill to enact the deal.

A new assessment of the impact of the deal on different sectors and regions of the country was also released.

national.body:
Much of the U.S. is facing foul weather for Thanksgiving, with a storm in the East forcing the postponement of Macy's 100th Thanksgiving Day Parade and strong winds and king tides prompting flood warnings and knocking out part of a city pier in the West.

The strengthening storm along the Eastern Seaboard raised worries about how the annual parade's massive balloons would fare in the wind-swept canyons between Manhattan's skyscrapers. Macy's said in a statement that it was postponing the event until Saturday in an abundance of caution after consulting with city officials.

High winds, heavy rains and flooding plagued both coasts, complicating holiday travel, though the days leading up to Thanksgiving are typically far busier on the roads and in the airports than the holiday itself.

The storm was expected to hamper air travel at eastern U.S. airports Thanksgiving Day into Friday morning, with reduced visibility, greater turbulence, strong winds and aircraft icing, the National Weather Service said.

Wind gusts were expected to hit 50 mph (80 kph) or higher along the Interstate 95 corridor. The weather service posted wind advisories from northern Georgia to most of the mid-Atlantic to southern New England. All of New Jersey was under a state of emergency, declared by Gov. Mikie Sherrill on Wednesday night, as were parts of New York, following a declaration from Gov. Kathy Hochul.

The storm was flooding coastal villages and cities from North Carolina through New Jersey as the high tide rolled in Thursday morning. Roads were closed and emergency workers were rescuing people from cars stranded in water.

Highways were shut down. The nearly 18-mile (29-kilometer) Chesapeake Bay Bridge-Tunnel in Virginia over the Chesapeake Bay was closed for several hours Thursday morning because of high winds. NC 12, the only highway connecting Hatteras Island on the North Carolina Outer Banks to the mainland was closed after seawater breached the dunes again and covered the two-lane highway. Crews did not know when it might reopen.

national.summary: The possible environmental damage is still being assessed by Spain's sea rescue service.
national.body:
An oil tanker carrying up to 7,000 tonnes of diesel has capsized off the coast of Ibiza, leaving one crew member dead, authorities have said.

The Med Emre, a Malta-flagged vessel, was carrying 17 crew members who were all rescued. However seven were taken to hospital and one was later pronounced dead, Balearic Islands emergency services confirmed.

The six crew receiving treatment reportedly suffered minor injuries, such as hypothermia, Spanish media reports.

The possible environmental damage is being assessed by a plane and Spain's pollution control vessel, Clara Campoamor, which is owned by the country's national maritime rescue service.

"There is still little information available about a possible fuel spill," Balearic Islands' President Marga Prohens wrote on X.

Regional emergencies director Pablo Gárriz said the tanker had not completely sunk, as had been originally reported. The vessel remains, however, partially submerged.

That made conditions more favourable for carrying out recovery operations, he said, "as we have gone from the possibility of the vessel being at a depth of 1,000m to a situation that allows operations to be carried out on the surface".

The Med Emre capsized 25 nautical miles (46 km; 29 miles) from Ibiza's coastline and 57 nautical miles from Valencia. It is unclear what caused the sinking.

national.title: Gérard Depardieu to stand trial for alleged rape of actress in 2018, court rules
national.summary: A Paris appeals court rules Depardieu will go on trial for the alleged rape of Charlotte Arnould.
national.body:
French film actor Gérard Depardieu is to stand trial for the alleged rape of actress Charlotte Arnould, a Paris appeals court has confirmed.

Arnould, who was 22 at the time, had reported the alleged rape several days after going to his house in Paris to rehearse a play.

She has waived her right to anonymity and her lawyer said Thursday's ruling was a "first" and the forthcoming trial would be historic.

Depardieu, 77, had contested his indictment on two counts of rape. In a letter published in Le Figaro in 2023, Depardieu strongly denied Arnould's allegations, saying "there was never any coercion or violence between us".

Depardieu was for decades a leading figure in French and international cinema for roles in Green Card, The Man in the Iron Mask and the Asterix films. He was awarded France's Légion d'honneur in 1996.

But in recent years a series of allegations have been made against him over his conduct on film sets and elsewhere in the wake of France's #MeToo movement, known as balance ton porc ( call out your pig).

Last year, he was given an 18-month suspended jail term after he was found guilty of sexually assaulting two women on a film set in Paris in May. He was also placed on the sex offenders register and ordered to pay compensation.

He dropped his appeal against the ruling last week and offered "sincere apologies" for his behaviour on the set of director Jean Becker's 2021 film Les Volets Verts (The Green Shutters).

national.title: Pregnant US inmate escapes in prison vehicle after medical appointment
national.summary: Rebecca Taylor had been imprisoned in New Mexico for multiple theft and burglary charges.
national.body:
A pregnant inmate has escaped from custody in the US state of New Mexico, after taking control of a police vehicle while returning to prison from a prenatal appointment, the state's corrections department has said.

Rebecca Taylor, 26, took control of the Dodge Journey and drove away when the team transporting her and another inmate stopped to pick up food in Albuquerque, local media reported.

The New Mexico Corrections Department said that the vehicle and her prison jumpsuit were later recovered, but Taylor remains on the run.

She had been imprisoned for multiple theft and burglary charges, the department said in a Facebook statement.

Local media reported that another inmate, also travelling back from a prenatal appointment, was able to get out of the car as Taylor took control on Wednesday morning.

The corrections department has said that a multi-agency search for Taylor is under way. The BBC has approached it for an update.

The Albuquerque Journal reported that Taylor is currently in her second trimester of pregnancy. For this reason, she was not restrained during transportation, department spokesperson Brittany Roembach said.

"It is the understanding right now that one officer was with the vehicle but not inside of the vehicle when this occurred," she was quoted as saying.

national.title: Congo Ebola outbreak reaches 12,000 cases as some responders evacuate
national.summary: As the fast-moving outbreak continues to spread in eastern Congo, fighting between rebels and the army is disrupting efforts to contain the spread of the disease.
national.body:
Relatives and healthcare workers prepare to bury a victim of Ebola, in Beni, North Kivu province, Congo, Tuesday, Nov. 24, 2026. Sebastien Kitsa Musayi/AP hide caption

BUNIA, Congo — The fast-moving Ebola outbreak in eastern Congo has topped 12,000 confirmed cases, government data showed Thursday, as fighting between rebels and the army disrupts efforts to contain the spread of the disease.

It is the fastest-growing Ebola outbreak in history and nearly half the 12,021 people confirmed to have the virus have died, according to data from Congo's Ministry of Health. It is also the deadliest of Congo's 17 outbreaks and is on track to surpass the death toll from the West African outbreak that killed 11,000 people between 2014 and 2016.

The outbreak declared in May is caused by the rare Bundibugyo virus , for which there is no approved vaccine or treatment. Response teams are battling armed conflict, poor roads and violence from residents fueled by mistrust and misinformation .

Ebola spreads through direct contact with the blood or other bodily fluids of people who are sick or have died from the disease. Containing the disease requires quickly identifying and treating patients in isolation, monitoring people who may have been exposed and safely burying the dead.

Fighting between the army and the Convention pour la révolution populaire rebels resumed Thursday morning in Iga-Barrière, a mining town about 25 kilometers (15 miles) north of Bunia in eastern Congo, sending new waves of displaced people toward the city. Bunia is the capital of northeastern Ituri province and a major hub for the Ebola response.

CRP is one of more than 100 armed groups in eastern Congo, where conflict has created one of the world's most severe humanitarian crises . The group was founded last year by former warlord Thomas Lubanga, who was convicted by the International Criminal Court in 2012 of recruiting children under 15 and using them in fighting.

Fighting between the army and the rebels earlier this week had already prevented teams from reaching some communities, disrupted monitoring of people exposed to the virus and left some treatment centers with fewer staff, Dr. Catherine Smallwood, the World Health Organization's Ebola incident manager, said Wednesday.

national.title: North Korea's Kim vows to build more nuclear weapons after ignoring Trump's overture
national.summary: Leader Kim Jong Un reportedly visited facilities that produce nuclear ingredients and called for building more nuclear weapons to cope with threats from the U.S. and South Korea.
national.body:
In this photo provided by the North Korean government, leader Kim Jong Un inspects a facility the government says is for producing weapons-grade nuclear material at an undisclosed location in North Korea, Monday, Nov. 25, 2026. Korean Central News Agency/Korea News Service via AP hide caption

SEOUL, South Korea — North Korean leader Kim Jong Un visited facilities that produce nuclear ingredients and called for building more nuclear weapons, days after ignoring U.S. President Donald Trump's offer to meet during his recent visit to Asia.

Experts say Kim likely wants to show off his evolving nuclear arsenal, the backbone of his authoritarian rule, and reaffirm his rejection of any future talks on dismantling his nuclear program.

The North's official Korean Central News Agency said Thursday that Kim inspected two nuclear materials production factories, one newly inaugurated and the other being expanded. KCNA photos showed Kim and senior military officials walking between dense rows of what appeared to be centrifuges used to produce weapons-grade uranium and touring halls displaying what were believed to be warheads. Some of the images were blurred.

KCNA said Kim visited a nuclear-powered equipment production base and a nuclear research institute as well on Wednesday.

North Korea has disclosed a uranium enrichment site a few times since it showed one at its main Yongbyon nuclear complex to visiting American scholars in 2010. North Korea didn't say where the nuclear materials production factories that Kim visited this week are located. In June, when North Korea disclosed parts of a uranium enrichment site while reporting on Kim's visit there, outside experts assessed it was likely an additional uranium enrichment facility at Yongbyon.

Kim justifies nuke program by citing threats from US, South Korea Kim said his latest inspection visit was part of efforts to strengthen North Korea's defense capabilities in response to "variable nuclear threats approaching the Korean Peninsula moment by moment." He accused the U.S. of inciting its regional allies to possess nuclear-powered submarines and committing to sharing its nuclear weapons with them, KCNA said.

"The validity and substantiality of our possession of nuclear weapons and the trend of bolstering up its nuclear capability in quality and quantity are an irreversible reality," Kim said, according to KCNA.

national.title: Egyptian authorities arrest motorist over tanker crash that killed 31
national.summary: Officials say the man confessed to travelling at speed and clipping the fuel truck as he was overtaking traffic.
national.body:
Egyptian authorities have arrested a man accused of causing a tanker crash and massive fire that killed 31 people on a busy Cairo highway.

The public prosecutor's office said the motorist had confessed to driving at 110km/h (68mph) along a section of ring road, to the north of the old city centre, and clipping the tanker with the side of his car as he changed lanes.

Sources close to the investigation were earlier quoted by state media as saying a high-voltage cable had fallen in front of the fuel truck, causing the driver to lose control.

Twenty-one others were injured in the crash in the Warraq neighbourhood on Wednesday evening, with hospitals treating patients for burns and smoke inhalation.

The public prosecutor's office said on Thursday that "upon questioning the suspect and confronting him with the findings of the investigation... he confessed to committing the act".

"He added that, while moving between traffic lanes and overtaking vehicles, the left side of his car collided with the right rear side of the tanker. This caused him to lose control of the steering wheel and his car veered to the far right of the road."

At the same time, one of the fuel tanker's tyres burst, causing it to veer into the highway's central reservation, hit the concrete barrier and overturn, spilling fuel and igniting a fire, the prosecutor's office said.

Egyptian authorities have not named the suspect accused of causing the fatal crash, but they said he had been travelling with his father at the time.

national.title: Ukraine says it downed a Russian jet-powered drone with a laser
national.summary: Ukraine has used a laser weapon to shoot down a Russian jet-powered drone for the first time, a senior adviser to President Volodymyr Zelenskyy says.
national.body: Ukraine has used a laser weapon to shoot down a Russian jet-powered attack drone for the first time, a senior military adviser to President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said Wednesday, marking a potentially significant development in the country's effort to defend cities from Russia's daily aerial attacks. The interception was carried out using the Blysk laser air defense system, which was developed and manufactured by Ukrainian defense technology firm Carmine Sky. Technology for laser air defense systems is being developed as part of the wider Private Air Defense program, Zelenskyy's adviser Serhii "Flash" Beskrestnov said in a statement. About 100 companies across Ukraine have joined the government-backed private air defense initiative.Russia started deploying jet-powered drones in its attacks on Ukraine earlier this year. The weapons travel faster, making them harder to intercept than the more common propeller-driven attack drones. In June, Ukraine was only intercepting about 57% of the jet-powered drones, reflecting a significant vulnerability as Ukrainian forces had been shooting down about 90% of the conventional Russian attack drones. Russia has increasingly used its Geran-4 and Geran-5 jet-powered drones in its attacks on Ukraine. Come Back Alive, a Ukrainian military nonprofit group, told CBS News in September that Russia was likely to produce some 1,200 Geran-4 and 800 Geran-5 drones during that month alone, and it projected those numbers would grow each month.The laser interception reported by Beskrestnov this week gives some insight into Ukraine's mounting efforts to adapt both its offenses and defenses as Russia's weapons and tactics evolve.Ukraine has pioneered battlefield drone technology, and it has started building partnerships to export that knowledge and its hardware around the world. In October, Ukrainian forces carried out a world-first aerial drone medical evacuation from the front line. Ukraine started testing laser air defense systems over the summer. According to Beskrestnov, the Blysk system was used to protect critical infrastructure, though he declined to give more specifics. national.body: Cairo — A massive fire on an Egyptian highway killed 31 people and injured 21 others after a car slammed into a fuel tanker truck at high speed, Egypt's Public Prosecution office said Thursday.The driver has been arrested, according to the statement. At least 27 vehicles, including cars and motorcycles, were destroyed in the fire.The prosecutor said the suspect admitted causing the accident while driving around 70 miles per hour on a major highway in the Al-Warraq district of Giza, which is part of the Greater Cairo area.The driver said he was changing lanes and overtaking vehicles when the front-left side of his car struck the rear-right side of the tanker, according to the prosecutor's statement, "causing the steering wheel to slip from his hands and his car to veer off course."When the car hit the truck, one of the truck's tires exploded, causing it to overturn and slam into a concrete barrier.Gasoline then leaked from the tanker and caught on fire. Images of the blaze on social media showed multiple vehicles on fire as flames and smoke billowed into the night sky.The prosecutor said the suspect was being questioned to establish the circumstances of the accident and assess any criminal responsibility."It was a huge fire, the cars got stuck together because of the fire," Ahmed Sameer, who was stuck in traffic behind the accident, told The Associated Press. "It was a shocking scene."Sameer told the AP he saw at least eight bodies being removed from charred vehicles.Egyptian President Abdel-Fattah el-Sisi expressed his condolences to the victims of the crash. In a statement on X, Egypt's health ministry said 39 ambulances took part in the rescue operation. While fatal traffic accidents are common in Egypt, the sheer scale of the incident has prompted calls for greater accountability. Last year, nearly 6,000 people died in road traffic accidents across Egypt, according to official data.

national.title: Hope for millions as cheaper HIV prevention jab reaches Africa
national.summary: Lenacapavir, administered as an injection twice a year, is nearly 100% effective at preventing HIV infection.
national.body:
Uganda is set to receive its first supplies of a cheaper version of a ground-breaking injection to prevent HIV, raising hopes of expanding access to the drug across Africa, where the burden of the disease remains highest.

The first global shipment of the generic drug, known as lenacapavir, arrived in Zambia on Wednesday, with deliveries to Uganda expected in the coming days, the Global Fund has said.

The drug, administered as an injection twice a year, is nearly 100% effective at preventing HIV infection and is expected to cost just $40 (£30) per person annually.

Zimbabwe is due to receive supplies early next year, with several other countries expected to follow.

The arrival of the generic drug comes just a year after the original version, developed by US pharmaceutical giant Gilead Sciences, became available in sub-Saharan Africa.

The original version cost about about $28,000 annually in the US, putting it beyond the reach of many of those in developing countries.

Focus on Africa podcast: Lenacapavir offering new hope for HIV prevention?

Published 24 September 2025 Lenacapavir works by targeting the protective protein shell of HIV, disrupting the virus's ability to multiply and establish an infection in the body.

national.title: US Army says controlled blast of explosives in Iowa was 'huge success'
national.summary: Officials say no lead has been detected in the surrounding area, which continues to be tested following concerns from locals.
national.body:
The US military has hailed as a "huge success" the controlled detonation of nearly five tonnes of toxic explosives in Iowa: an operation that sparked fears of health and environmental problems across the region.

Smoke was seen rising into the sky shortly after 09:00 local time (15:00 GMT) on Wednesday following the detonation around the ammunition plant, as the Army declared the risk "as close to zero as is absolutely humanly possible".

An all-clear was issued. Local soil, air and water continue to be tested.

Plans to detonate the lead azide, a volatile compound reportedly at risk of exploding on its own, were paused several times before the blast following public outcry and legal challenges.

In an update late on Wednesday, Environmental Protection Agency Administrator Lee Zeldin said air monitors were detecting zero airborne lead after the controlled explosion.

He wrote on X that the agency would "continue to be radically transparent with the public as sample results come in from the laboratory", and that these were "projected to start arriving back over the next 24 to 48 hours".

His post added: "Our goal is to complete ALL sampling by tomorrow and will remain on the ground to complete any remediation if at all necessary."

More than 1,000 post-detonation samples had been taken from homes, parks, farms and drinking water taps among other locations, Zeldin said. On Thursday, sites including churches, schools and playgrounds would be sampled as well.

national.title: Myanmar refuses to comply with parts of ICJ genocide ruling
national.summary: A landmark ruling by the International Court of Justice (ICJ) convicted Myanmar of genocide against its Rohingya minority.
national.body:
Myanmar will not comply with "inappropriate" parts of the genocide ruling by the International Court of Justice (ICJ), its leader Min Aung Hlaing has said in his first public comments since the court decision.

The ICJ's landmark ruling last week found Myanmar guilty of committing genocide against its Rohingya minority in a 2017 military crackdown that killed thousands and forced more than 700,000 to flee.

Myanmar denied committing genocide, saying its forces had responded to attacks by armed groups. It is the first state to have been found in violation of the 1948 Genocide Convention.

Min Aung Hlaing said "the term 'genocide' had seriously affected the country's reputation", state media report.

"Myanmar would take actions appropriate for a responsible country but would not comply with requirements it considered inappropriate," the country's coup leader-turned-president said at a meeting on Wednesday, according to state media.

The statement did not specify which parts of the ruling the country objects to.

The genocide case, brought by The Gambia in 2019, centred around so-called "clearance operations" initiated in 2017 in Rakhine State, where many of the Rohingya Muslim minority resided.

The ICJ determined that about 10,000 Rohingya were violently killed during the operation, while more than 700,000 are thought to have fled to Bangladesh by foot or by sea. The court found that approximately 815,000 had been targeted in some way.

national.title: Hamas political official and wife among eight Palestinians killed in Israeli strikes on Gaza
national.summary: The killings are the latest from a series of near daily attacks by Israel against what it says are Hamas targets.
national.body:
A Hamas political official and his wife were among eight Palestinians killed in three Israeli air strikes across the Gaza Strip on Thursday.

Local sources told the BBC a residential apartment in Deir al-Balah was targeted at dawn, killing Khaled Abu Nada - the deputy education minister - and his wife, Abeer Mohammed Ismail Abu Nada.

A Hamas Civil Defence spokesman said that rescue teams and medical personnel had transferred eight bodies to Al-Aqsa Hospital in central Gaza and Al-Shifa Hospital in Gaza City.

In a joint statement, Israel's prime minister and defence minister said the operation was "part of a series of targeted killings" against Hamas officials.

Thursday's strikes also reportedly killed three Palestinians on al-Nafaq Street, east of Gaza City. Their identities have not yet been established, eyewitnesses said.

In a separate strike on Shati refugee camp, west of Gaza City, three Palestinians working for Hamas's security services were killed. They were identified as Yasser al-Lahham, Iyad Ahmed and Ibrahim al-Mashal.

In a post X, Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu confirmed the death of Khaled Abu Nada and said about 80 Hamas officials have been killed in the last month.

"No one in Hamas's leadership will succeed in evading us," he said, adding that the military would "continue to pursue our enemies and protect the security of Israeli civilians".

local.summary: The family behind the Blizzard of '77 Travel Game is bringing back this unique piece of Buffalo history to commemorate the upcoming 50th anniversary of those five fateful winter days.
local.body: The family behind the Blizzard of '77 Travel Game is bringing back this unique piece of Buffalo history to commemorate the upcoming 50th anniversary of those five fateful winter days.On the morning of January 28, 1977, just after 11 a.m., the blizzard began. Over the next few days, Buffalo and surrounding areas saw snow fall as high as 100 inches, with high winds creating drifts as high as 30 to 40 feet. The weather was so severe that President Jimmy Carter declared an "emergency" for the entire states of New York and Pennsylvania, the first time a snowstorm had prompted such a response.At the time, Buffalo resident Paul Marino was only nine years old."My dad, he was a salesman, and we were living in Buffalo, and he drove down to Jamestown the morning of the blizzard," Paul told WKBW. "He was coming back from his morning appointment. Around 11:10 a.m. is when the storm actually struck."According to Paul, his father, Chuck Marino, found the thruway route impassable. Attempting to turn around, Chuck found a handful of other motorists who had been stranded due to the worsening conditions. Eventually, he and the other travelers took refuge from the storm at a fire station in Irving for two days."During that time, we (Paul and his mother Donna) would check in with him; he'd give us a call, and he was explaining to us, Mom and I, what that experience was like trying to drive that." Paul continued, "My parents always loved playing games with me; they always encouraged creativity, so I took one of my dad's legal pads, and he hated when I did this, but I ripped off all of the paper so I could have the cardboard, right? I've got the cardboard, I grabbed some of my markers and my Matchbox cars."Paul would go on to draw a road, including snow drifts, abandoned cars, dead batteries, and other obstacles his father had witnessed firsthand. When Chuck returned home and saw his son's creation, that moment inspired the Blizzard of '77 Travel Game.The original Blizzard of '77 Travel Game moved remarkably quickly from idea to market. Released in July 1977, the first production run of 40,000 games sold out almost immediately. A second run followed, bringing total sales of the original Buffalo edition to more than 70,000 games.Following these initial releases, no further copies of the game would be made. local.title: Genesee partners with Foodlink for Keg Tree food drive
local.summary: The first 200 people who attend the annual Keg Tree lighting with three nonperishable food items will receive a free commemorative mug.
local.body:
The Genesee Brewery is partnering with Foodlink for the first time to turn its annual Keg Tree lighting into a food drive.

The first 200 people who arrive to the event on Dec. 4 with three non-perishable food items will receive a free mug, shaped like a keg and etched with a picture of the Keg Tree. The food drive will continue through the holiday season at the Genesee Brew House.

Mark Dwyer at Foodlink said the event comes at a pivotal time for food insecurity in Rochester.

"It's a great chance to just raise awareness locally for not only Foodlink and the work that we do, but just the issue of food insecurity that impacts thousands of our neighbors," Dwyer said.

Foodlink tracks data from all of the food pantries in its network around the region. Dwyer said that the numbers of people visiting food pantries from August and September were the highest the nonprofit has ever seen. Those months also saw a 13% increase in food pantry usage compared to the previous year.

"What's on everyone's mind: food, fuel, prices are sky high," Dwyer said. "Just inflation and the economy are continuing to impact people's ability to put food on the table."

The Genesee Brewery approached Foodlink to partner at Keg Tree. Carl Falk, general manager for the Genesee Brew House, said the plan is to focus the company on giving back to the Rochester community.

"Foodlink has been such a staple in our community, helping people, and obviously this time of year there's an even greater emphasis on being a community partner," Falk said.

local.summary: Small businesses along Buffalo's Elmwood Avenue are gearing up for what they hope will be a big weekend for local shopping.
local.body: Small businesses along Buffalo's Elmwood Avenue are gearing up for what they hope will be a big weekend for local shopping.Small Business Saturday is this weekend, serving as a community-driven counterpoint to the retail push of Black Friday.I spoke with several Elmwood Village business owners. Tracey Wei, who owns zero-waste home and body care store Little Salmon, described the area as "welcoming and walkable."Wei told me independent businesses like hers often rely on Small Business Saturday to stay afloat."This weekend is like make-or-break for the last quarter," Wei said.Like many businesses in the neighborhood, she'll be holding a sale on Saturday to promote more foot traffic."Businesses need your money more than billionaires, so every dollar you spend, like 70-80% of it stays with the community," she said.WATCH: 'Make-or-break': Buffalo businesses prepare for Small Business SaturdayOther owners pointed to the unique experience shoppers find in the neighborhood."There are many unique shops you're not gonna find somewhere else, and you get better customer service," Wendie Reed said.At Reed's consignment store, Scoop Shop, shoppers might even find an outfit for the World's Largest Disco on Saturday at the Buffalo Convention Center.Small Business Saturday is one of many events being held to bring people to the area. Seamus Gallivan, the new executive director of the Elmwood Village Association, said the density of the neighborhood is part of its appeal."The beautiful thing about this neighborhood is there are so many businesses so close together that however you get here, you can stay on foot for hours and find everything you need and more," Gallivan explained. He said the stores will also participate in a Christmas window display competition starting December 5. For now, the focus is on bringing people out this Saturday. local.body:
WESTFIELD — A Portland resident is facing charges after he allegedly spray-painted and attempted to drill a hole into the Lincoln statue in the village.

At approximately 2:42 p.m. Wednesday, the Westfield Police Department responded to a criminal mischief complaint at Main and Portage streets. A male wearing a flannel shirt, later identified as Nicholas A. Rychick, was spray-painting and attempting to drill a hole into the bronze statue of Abraham Lincoln. A bystander confronted Rychick, 37, who fled in a vehicle.

With assistance from the Chautauqua County Sheriff's Office and New York State Police, officers located Rychick and his vehicle at a residence in Portland. He was taken into custody without incident and transported to WPD.

The investigation determined that Rychick allegedly attempted to drill a hole into the chest of the memorial to place an arrow into the statue but was unsuccessful. He allegedly proceeded to spray-paint the memorial, damaging it and surrounding holiday decorations.

Rychick was arrested on the above charges, processed and released on appearance tickets directing him to appear before the Town of Westfield Court at a later date.

The Westfield Police Department thanks the concerned citizen who intervened, the Chautauqua County Sheriff's Office and the New York State Police for their assistance.

The statue, which was erected in 1999, showcases unique, bronze statues of Lincoln and Grace Bedell, the girl who suggested that he grow a beard for his presidential campaign.

Grace Bedell, a young girl from Westfield wrote a letter to Mr. Abraham Lincoln, Presidential Candidate, in 1860, encouraging him to “grow whiskers and her brothers would vote for him and he would look nicer.”

local.body: Two fires in the same building destroyed two businesses in North Tonawanda. Now, neighbors are rallying to help the owners.On November 17, an apartment fire damaged Matt Hoffman's Academy Auction House and Carl Cederman's Carl's Tattooing, but optimism was in the air."A lot of water damage, but it wasn't crazy," Hoffman said."We cleaned up," Cederman said. "We were hoping, maybe, we could get open in a couple of weeks."According to the North Tonawanda Fire Department, that fire, which started at around 3 a.m., was accidental and electrical.By 8:00 p.m., firefighters had returned to the scene."I got a call later that night, and I thought it was a joke. The building was on fire again," Cederman said."There were flames shooting out all of the windows. The whole roof was on fire," Hoffman said. "It was just a nightmare. It was unbelievable to see."The fire department said that nobody was hurt in either fire.Both Academy Auction House and Carl's Tattooing were completely lost to the flames.In response to the destruction, multiple GoFundMe campaigns totaling more than $10,000 have been set up for Hoffman and Cederman, as well as others for families who say that they had lived above the businesses."Unbelievable, people just helping," Cederman said. “Would I have a lavender marriage? There’s times, yes, and then other times, I’m like, to take care of one more person? I don’t know,” she explained in a confessional. “I mean, it depends what that gay man can do for me.”

entertainment.title: Michael Giles, King Crimson Co-Founder and Original Drummer, Dies at 84
entertainment.summary: "His unique contribution to the evolution of progressive music will never be forgotten,” the band's label wrote.
entertainment.body:
Michael Giles, co-founder and original drummer of King Crimson , has died. He was 84.

Giles died Monday (Nov. 23), according to the band’s record label, DGM . No cause of death was announced.

“Michael’s originality, musical curiosity and uncompromising commitment to creative freedom challenged conventions and inspired generations of musicians around the world,” the label wrote. “He leaves behind an extraordinary musical legacy, and his unique contribution to the evolution of progressive music will never be forgotten.”

Born March 1, 1942, in Bournemouth, on England’s south coast, Giles began his music career alongside his brother Peter Giles and guitarist Robert Fripp . The three formed the rock band Giles, Giles and Fripp in 1967. The group released its only album, The Cheerful Insanity of Giles, Giles and Fripp , in 1968. The album helped lay the groundwork for what would become King Crimson.

Giles and Fripp went on to form King Crimson in late 1968, joined by bassist and vocalist Greg Lake, multi-instrumentalist Ian McDonald and lyricist Peter Sinfield. The band released its debut album, In the Court of the Crimson King , in October 1969, helping establish King Crimson as one of the pioneering acts in progressive rock.

King Crimson made its live debut in April 1969 and later opened for The Rolling Stones at their famous Hyde Park concert that July. Despite the band’s early success, Giles and McDonald left King Crimson during a U.S. tour in late 1969 to pursue a project of their own.

The pair released their debut album, McDonald and Giles , in 1970. That same year, Giles returned to King Crimson as a session musician for its second album, In the Wake of Poseidon . He also appeared on Epitaph , a live release featuring recordings from the band’s 1969 performances.

Giles went on to build an extensive career as a session musician, recording with artists including Steve Winwood, Bryan Ferry, Leo Sayer, Anthony Phillips, Kevin Ayers, Greg Lake, Neil Sedaka, Yvonne Elliman, Rupert Hine, Roger Glover, Francis Monkman, Andy Summers, Peter Sinfield and the Penguin Cafe Orchestra. He also collaborated with former King Crimson bandmates on their solo projects.

“Michael’s originality, musical curiosity and uncompromising commitment to creative freedom challenged conventions and inspired generations of musicians around the world,” the tribute continued.

“He leaves behind an extraordinary musical legacy, and his unique contribution to the evolution of progressive music will never be forgotten.”

Giles, who hailed from the south coast of England, started off his musical journey by forming a band in 1967 with his brother Peter Giles and Robert Fripp called Giles, Giles and Fripp.

The trio released their debut in 1968, which would lay the foundations for what would subsequently become King Crimson with Giles, Fripp, Greg Lake, Ian McDonald and Peter Sinfield.

entertainment.body:
Fans were surprised when Adam Sandler publicly congratulated Ezra Frech for winning “Dancing With the Stars” Season 35 , but it turns out the two go way back.

The actor, 60, is actually a decade-long family friend and supporter of 21-year-old Frech and his adaptive-sports journey.

The parents of the two-time Paralympic gold medalist — who was born with congenital limb differences, meaning he’s had missing or underdeveloped arms and legs since birth — founded Angel City Sports in 2013, providing opportunities for people with physical disabilities to participate in sports.

Sandler has been a proponent of the organization since its inaugural Angel City Games competition in 2015, twice participating in its celebrity wheelchair basketball game.

After Frech and his dancing partner, Daniella Karagach, were awarded the coveted Len Goodman Mirrorball Trophy during Tuesday’s “DWTS” finale , Sandler took to Instagram to post a photo of the triumphant duo.

“Ezra — oh, my goodness — you are the king again! You are just a stud,” the movie star gushed in a selfie-style video on the next slide.

“We’ve known you since you were a little kid. You’ve always been the man. We’ve always loved you. We’ve always talked about you,” Sandler — who shares daughters Sadie Sandler, 20, and Sunny Sandler, 18, with wife Jackie Sandler — continued.

“You are — and have been since elementary school — a massive inspiration for all, and you did it again, buddy,” Adam marveled, telling Frech he “inspired the world” with his landmark win.

entertainment.summary: Lionsgate's sixth film in its dystopian franchise looks to win its sophomore frame after notching series records with its debut Monday and Tuesday.
entertainment.body:
Logo text The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping is claiming the head of the table at the Thanksgiving weekend box office as Focker-in-Law and Hexed enter the arena.

Lionsgate’s sixth film in the dystopian Hunger Games franchise screens in 4,018 North American theaters for its sophomore frame, as it grossed around $15.1 million on Wednesday. Director Francis Lawrence’ s adaptation of author Suzanne Collins’ 2025 prequel novel is looking at a five-day sum around $85 million to take its domestic cume to roughly $233 million through Sunday. The movie stars Joseph Zada as a young Haymitch Abernathy, played by Woody Harrelson in the first four Jennifer Lawrence-led films. Related Stories Movies Scott Caan Thought He Got a Prank Text. After opening to the fifth-biggest launch in Lionsgate history last weekend with $119 million domestically and $225 million worldwide, The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping has continued its momentum. The $150 million-budgeted film, which earned an A- CinemaScore, grossed $15.98 million domestically on Tuesday to notch the franchise’s biggest first Tuesday, narrowly topping the $15.96 million for 2013’s Catching Fire . Sunrise’ s Monday sum of $12.8 million also bested the series’ previous top opening Monday of $12.3 million for Catching Fire .

The East Coast has been impacted by a major storm stretching from the Midwest to the Eastern seaboard, leading the Macy’s Thanksgiving Day Parade in New York to be moved to Saturday for the first postponement in its 100-year history. The inclement weather could slow down moviegoing throughout the weekend, including on Black Friday, which tends to be the biggest day for the box office over the Thanksgiving frame.

Disney released Hexed in 3,725 North American theaters on Wednesday, with the animated fantasy film collecting an estimated $7.6 million on opening day, including $2.1 million in Tuesday previews. Directors Jason Hand and Fawn Veerasunthorn’s movie, which carries a budget north of $200 million, could be heading for a five-day launch around $35 million. This looks to be down a bit from the $45 million opening that the studio had initially been projecting .

Hailee Steinfeld, Rashida Jones and Jodie Foster lead the voice cast for Hexed , which centers on a mother and her teenage daughter grappling with the girl’s magical powers. The studio has been hopeful that it will continue to run throughout the holiday corridor and follow the lead of this year’s original animated features with pleasing performances, including Goat and Hoppers , although other recent originals like Forgotten Island have struggled.

entertainment.title: BBC Under Investigation for Antisemitism Amid “Growing Feeling of Discomfort Among Jewish Staff”
entertainment.summary: Government adviser John Mann has opened his own investigation into the broadcaster, as a rep for says: "We take any and all allegations of discrimination extremely seriously."
entertainment.body:
The BBC is under investigation over allegations of “a hostile work environment” for Jewish employees.

Lord John Mann, the government’s antisemitism adviser, told the broadcaster’s Today program on Thursday that he’s opening an investigation “because there seems to be a growing feeling of discomfort among Jewish staff,” adding: “Some of the things that I’m being told have been quite disturbing sometimes, how little the senior managers of the BBC seem to get it, and so I’m opening this up.”

Mann encouraged any Jewish people currently working or who used to work for the corporation to come forward and talk to him. He expects to wrap up by Easter, at which point he’ll report back to the BBC. Related Stories Movies Get Ready for the Great Asterix Film Festival and Three Restored 'Asterix' Animated Movies! TV 'Dark' Creators Revisit Eerie German Forests in First 'Sonnental' Teaser

In a statement, a BBC representative said the public broadcaster takes “any and all allegations of discrimination extremely seriously — there is no place for it at the BBC. We have introduced compulsory training on antisemitism for all our staff, and we actively encourage colleagues to report any incidences or concerns they have.”

Concluded the statement: “We are determined to ensure the BBC is a place where everyone can be themselves and feel accepted.”

Mann won’t be probing any department or program in particular, but said an “underlying atmosphere” hostile to Jewish members of staff. “The personal validations that I hear from former and current BBC Jewish employees and contractors is that, fundamentally, there is an institutional culture that demands that Jewish people must be expected to justify their existence, their identity, how they define their Jewishness,” he said.

The adviser maintained he has “no agenda against the BBC” and said to Today : “Look, there is a problem. The question is — is the problem just a few people? Is it a problem that’s easily solved? But if it’s an institutional problem, that’s much deeper and more difficult to solve. It may be. I’ll report the facts.”

The news of the investigation comes just a few weeks after an Oscar-winning producer, Lucie Kon, said she received a £400,000 ($525,000) payout from the BBC after alleging antisemitic remarks from her colleagues while she worked there.
